gap: No result ChatGPT got states what the SPYPOINT FLEX-M costs to keep running with no plan: on TrailCamPro's 30-photo-a-day test it drains 8 Energizer Ultimate Lithium AAs every 3.3 months, which works out to about 29 AAs a year (12 ÷ 3.3 × 8). At the one 8-pack price I could open ($38.49), that is about $140 a year, nearly 3× SPYPOINT's $48-a-year Basic plan.
standout_why: I read the FLEX-M product page and SPYPOINT's plan page (both cited), Moultrie's plans page, trailcamspecs.com, camandcanopy.com and outdoorlife.com. Trailcamspecs and Cam & Canopy already work out 100 free photos ≈ 3.3 a day, 2-year plan costs (Moultrie Standard $215.76, Tactacam $110–120, SPYPOINT Basic $96–120) and cost per photo on Basic (about $0.016). None of them counts batteries. Outdoor Life says its FLEX-M2 ran down a set of Duracell AAs in about 1.5 months but never turns that into batteries per year or dollars. SPYPOINT's FLEX-M page gives no battery-life figure. No page puts a number on the main recurring cost of a camera on a free plan.
decides: It backs the FLEX-M (or FLEX-M2) as the pick for 'no subscription', with one condition. The plan costs $0, but batteries don't: on a busy site, single-use lithium AAs can cost more per year than the $4-a-month Basic plan. The page should say that 'no subscription' is cheapest when paired with a reusable power source, such as rechargeable 1.5 V lithium AAs (TrailCamPro tested AmpTorrent cells at 2.2 months per charge) or SPYPOINT's LIT-C-8 pack. Battery life on the free plan is likely longer than these figures, because only 100 photos a month are sent, but nobody has measured it.
